Accepted.description:
Every step ran and every requirement is met.

`anchors` holds each newest period the run's rolling steps were written
from, in the order resolved, one for each group of rolling steps
(`compiler.rolling.anchor_groups`), with groups over the same series and
frames sharing one. Empty when no step rolls.

AnchorResult.description:
The newest period one group of a run's rolling steps stands on, as
`resolve_anchor` answered it (`compiler.rolling.anchor_groups`).

`anchor_key` names the stored resolution every rolling call of the group
was sent, `period` is the newest period held by at least half of the
series of each population, and `left_out` the series that hold no value
at it. `steps` are the rolling steps of every group that stands on it
(`AnchorGroup.steps`), `roots` the retrieval steps of those groups
(`AnchorGroup.roots`), and `populations` the populations the period was
taken over, spelled the way the retrieved frames spell their columns
(`compiler.frame_columns.bound_populations`). The run writes all three;
`resolve_anchor` does not send them.

detail.description: A human-readable explanation of this finding.

entities.description: The entities of the one retrieved series a `window_short` or `coverage_gaps` finding is about.

found.description: What was actually found, when this finding compares an expectation to an observation.

magnitude.description: The largest absolute value the one retrieved series a `window_short` or `coverage_gaps` finding is about holds in any period, which ranks the series an answer names.

required.description: What was required, when this finding compares an expectation to an observation.

requirement_id.description: The requirement this finding is about.

severity.description: How this finding bears on the requirement: error, warning or info.

stat_var.description: The StatVar of the one retrieved series a `window_short` or `coverage_gaps` finding is about.

EvidenceRecord.description:
One requirement's evidence: the frame that carries it and what the checks found.

`gaps` holds the findings the requirement accepts -- years missing under
`report_gaps`, a named entity the retrieval left out, a unit the source
did not state -- so an answer built on this evidence can say what it
rests on.

FrameRef.description:
Names one frame by the `{spec_id, content_version}` pair a tool reply gives.

A data or analysis tool's reply gives both values. `spec_id` is a dataset's
`spec_` id or an analysis result's `ops_` id, and `content_version` is the
matching `cv_` or `ocv_` value.
FrameRef.title: FrameRef

LeftOutSeries.description:
One series counted for the newest period that holds no value at it.

`root` indexes the populations `resolve_anchor` was sent, in their
canonical order, and `coordinates` is the series' value in each of its
columns.

MethodChoiceNeeded.description:
A tool refused with a choice only the planner can make with the user.

`candidates` is whatever the refusal offered to choose from, verbatim.
`also_stopped` names the wave's other stops, wave order, when this one
is the wave's first and so the one a run raises (`executor.run._Run.execute`).
`completed` and `evidence` hold the steps that finished before the stop
and the evidence their retrievals recorded, in the plan's own step order.
`answers` holds, by step id, each finished terminal step's frame that
passed the answer check an accepted run applies (`executor.run._Run.
_answer_refusal`). `anchors` holds the newest period of each group of
rolling steps the run resolved before it stopped.

Period.description: An inclusive range of calendar years.

end.description: The last year this period covers.

start.description: The first year this period covers.

RediscoveryNeeded.description:
A retrieval's source needs discovering again; a bare retry would only repeat the refusal.

Discovering the source again is the translator's job under a new plan
revision, not a retry this loop can make on its own. `requirement_id`
and `spec_id` name the requirement and the source the step was approved
to retrieve, read off its `EvidenceBinding`; a step without one has
nothing to rediscover, so its refusal comes back as `Refused` instead.
`also_stopped` names the wave's other stops, wave order, when this one
is the wave's first and so the one a run raises (`executor.run._Run.execute`).
`completed` and `evidence` hold the steps that finished before the stop
and the evidence their retrievals recorded, in the plan's own step order.
`answers` holds, by step id, each finished terminal step's frame that
passed the answer check an accepted run applies (`executor.run._Run.
_answer_refusal`). `anchors` holds the newest period of each group of
rolling steps the run resolved before it stopped.

Refused.description:
The run stopped: what stopped it, where, and what was said.

`also_stopped` names the wave's other stops, wave order, when this one
is the wave's first and so the one a run raises (`executor.run._Run.execute`).
`completed` and `evidence` hold the steps that finished before the stop
and the evidence their retrievals recorded, in the plan's own step order.
`answers` holds, by step id, each finished terminal step's frame that
passed the answer check an accepted run applies (`executor.run._Run.
_answer_refusal`). `anchors` holds the newest period of each group of
rolling steps the run resolved before it stopped.

`spec_id` names the source a `REQUIREMENT_UNMET` stop read, when the
requirement has a binding, as a `RediscoveryNeeded` does. Other stops leave
it unset. A replan avoids the source of a `Refused` stop only when an error
finding says its unit is unverified and found no unit text
(`harness.planner_adapter._SOURCE_FAULT_CODES`).

`retryable` says whether a later attempt can get past a
`TRANSPORT_FAILED` stop: `False` when the tool surface reported a failure
no retry changes (`compiler.surface.ToolSurfaceUnavailableError`), such as
a server it does not cover. It is `True` for every other stop.

SeriesEntity.description:
One entity of a retrieved series, as its statistics name it.

`role` and `ref` are the series' own; `label` is the name the approved
source gives `ref`, `None` where it gives none.

label.description: The approved source's name for `ref`, when it names one.

ref.description: The entity's value in that column.

role.description: The series' role column for this entity.

Severity.description: How a finding bears on the requirement.

StepRecord.description:
One step that ran: what it called, how many attempts it took, what it produced.

`row_count`, `role_keys` and `stat_var_count` are the row count, the
frame's role columns and the distinct StatVars a successful call
declared in its own `structured_content`, or `None` when it declared
none. `get_data`, whose structured result is a `Manifest`, declares no
`rows`, and declares `role_keys` and `stat_var_count` whenever it read
the frame. `dropped_key_count` and `right_dropped_key_count` are how many
keys of its first and second input the call declared it left out of its
result (`executor.artifacts.declared_dropped_key_counts`): the numerator
keys a keyed `quotient_of` or `share_of` found nothing to divide by, and
each side's entities a `join` matched in no period. Both are 0 for every
other call, and `right_dropped_key_count` for every call but a `join`.
`ranked_before_limit` is how many entries a `rank` call ranked before its
`limit` cut them (`executor.artifacts.declared_ranked_before_limit`),
`None` when the call set no limit.

`frame_ref` is the pair later steps read the frame by. `manifest_ref` is
the manifest's own pair for a `get_data` step whose `frame_ref` differs
from it (a frame minted with extra columns,
`executor.artifacts.manifest_frame_ref`), and `None` otherwise.

ToolFailure.description:
A tool's refusal, typed off the raw MCP payload.

`code` and `retry_mode` are read against the five sets above, not
against a closed enum here -- the served vocabulary belongs to
`data_mcp.tool_errors.ToolErrorCode` and `analysis_mcp.tool_errors.ToolErrorCode`,
and this model exists to stop `classify.py` and its callers from
indexing an untyped mapping, not to duplicate those enums.

ToolId.description: A tool, by the server that serves it and its name there.

InputManifest.description: The run's retrieved inputs, sealed before any derived step runs.

ManifestEntry.description:
One retrieved root input at the exact version the run read. One source
may be read at several versions, by retrievals of different arguments.

ParameterOrigin.description:
Where a `RequestAuthorisation`'s recipe parameter came from: `recorded`
when the harness checked it against what the conversation recorded,
`model_stated` when it was the model's reading of the user's words.
ParameterOrigin.title: ParameterOrigin

PendingHold.description:
Why a run's publication is unfinished, and when a retry may succeed.
`code` is the fault's code; `reason` its text, which stays in the ledger.

PlanApproval.description:
A user's approval of one Plan revision, the authorisation every new run is
admitted under.

Publication.description:
Where a terminal result stands on durable publication. A root `spec_`
frame needs none; a derived `ops_` frame is `required` until published with
its replay recipe.
Publication.title: Publication

RequestAuthorisation.description:
The harness's authorisation of a request to run one reviewed recipe
without a plan. Stored runs carry it, so `RunRecord` reads it and a run
admitted under it is carried on like any other (`executor.run.resume_run`);
`new_run` takes a `PlanApproval`, so no new run is admitted under it.
`parameter_origins` names where each recipe parameter came from.

ResultFrame.description: One terminal frame a run produced: a root `spec_` frame or a derived `ops_` one.

SourcePolicy.description:
Which source definitions a run may read, and which of their versions.

`sources` are root `spec_` ids, held sorted and unique so two policies
naming the same sources digest the same. `latest` lets retrieval resolve
whatever version each source holds when it runs; the sealed manifest
records the versions it found.

StepAttempt.description:
One dispatch of one step's tool, recorded before the call goes out.
`attempt` counts from 1 per step.

run_record.description:
Everything durable about one run. `submission_digest` is
`submission_digest()` of the submission and source policy the run
executes. `outcome` is what its computation came to, as the executor
states it, recorded once with `Publishing` or `Fail`. `resumes` counts
how often the unfinished run was carried on (`Resume`). `delivered` says
no later turn carries a completed run on: the conversation recorded the
hand-back of its result, or `undelivered` reached the delivery bound
(`Undelivered`). `undelivered` counts the turns that carried a completed
run on without delivering its result.
